thread:
sam: Acme reports our JSON mode produced a parse error when the stream ended mid-object. They see 'Unexpected token , at position 512' in their consumer. Started after a load-balancer tweak.
maria: Can you drop their minimal repro or the raw chunks they received? need a short reproducer to validate.
sam: Logs from their proxy show these chunks (verbatim):

```
chunk: 60
{"results": [ { "id": 1, "value": "a" },
chunk: 32
 { "id": 2, "value": "b" },
chunk: 18
 { "id": 3, "value": "c"
// connection closed abruptly by upstream, no final closing bracket or CRLF
```

They said their JSON parser errors when the final "]}" is missing.
maria: interesting. Could be edge flush/connection close trimming the final bytes. Did they have any intermediate proxies (CF, nginx)?
sam: yes — CF + internal LB. They also tried reproducing with curl and saw a truncated tail. Example they used:

```
curl --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/generate?mode=json-stream" --http1.1 -v
```
and the response body ended mid-object.
devon: probable cause: upstream closed socket before kernel flushed final buffered TCP segment. In chunked responses we expect final 0-length chunk + CRLF. If the last CRLF isn't flushed, some clients read incomplete frame. Edge (CF) has been observed to send a FIN right after last payload without waiting for flush.
anna: Repro idea: run a tiny server that writes partial objects then closes the socket to mimic the faulty behavior. If we hit the same parse error, it's on the network path. Also capture our server's write/flush timeline and request-id.
maria: can you paste a minimal python repro you used? I'll run it locally.
sam: here's a minimal python server I used to simulate abrupt close — drops final bytes intentionally:

```
# python3 abrupt_stream.py
import socket, time
s = socket.socket()
s.bind(('127.0.0.1', 9001))
s.listen(1)
conn, _ = s.accept()
payload = (
  'HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\n'
  'Content-Type: application/json\r\n'
  'Transfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n'
  '60\r\n{"results": [ {"id":1,"v":"a"},\n'
  '20\r\n{"id":2,"v":"b"}\r\n'
  # intentionally omit the final chunk and closing brackets
)
conn.send(payload.encode())
# short pause then close without sending final 0 chunk
time.sleep(0.2)
conn.close()
s.close()
```

This reproduces the parser error locally with a standard JSON parser.
devon: good repro. Next steps: check our runtime's shutdown path for streaming responses. Ensure we flush stdout socket buffers and write final chunk before closing connection. Also look for any codepath that calls socket.shutdown(SHUT_WR) then closes immediately.
maria: I'll run the same repro against prod-sim node and add tcpdump to capture last bytes + FIN timing.
support-bot: Incident ticket INC-12345 created (severity: high) — assigned to devon. Relevant logs attached.
anna: small mitigation: for structured/json mode, we could send a small end-sentinel (e.g., "\n--END-OF-JSON--\n") that the client can strip if parser fails. Not ideal but reduces user impact while we fix.
devon: agree as a temporary mitigation. But first: find whether it's our upstream close or CF. If CF, we need to engage edge team. I'll instrument with socket-level timestamps and compare server write timestamp vs FIN.
maria: scheduled brief triage 11:30. I'll post results after tcpdump. :calendar: :mag_right:
sam: pinged customer with repro steps and asked for a packet capture if possible. they said they'll try. thanks folks. :thumbsup:
